QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_7

question.text: Sapphire Angel Fund, a sub-category of Category I AIF, is evaluating a follow-on round. The fund has INR 120 crore of investible capital. Under current SEBI (AIF) Regulations governing Angel Funds, which of the following is the MAXIMUM investment the fund can make in a single investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 / Table 6.1 specifies that Angel Funds must invest a minimum of INR 10 lakh and not more than INR 25 crore in a particular investee company. The 25% general Cat I/II concentration cap and the 10% Cat III cap do NOT govern Angel Funds — Angel Funds have their own bespoke floor and ceiling. The Trap: INR 10 lakh (Option A) is the per-investee MINIMUM, not maximum. Options C and D apply general Cat I/II/III caps that don't govern Angel Funds. Accredited-investor-only funding and the special per-investee rupee cap are Angel-Fund-specific carve-outs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A Cat I/II Distributor exam tests Angel Fund investor eligibility; XIX-C additionally tests the per-investee rupee caps since the Manager operates within them daily.
